item.title: Foxborough town officials deny there's a deal in place over World Cup security costs
item.description: Boston's FIFA World Cup organizing committee offers financial assurances to Foxborough select board for security costs for hosting the soccer tournament this summer, in hopes the board will approve an entertainment license that would allow the games to take place.

item.title: Why 'KPop Demon Hunters' is everywhere
item.description: 'KPop Demon Hunters' is one of the biggest movies on Netflix. It’s also an Oscar nominee that’s spawned chart-topping singles. How K-pop and K-culture became an irresistible global phenomenon.

item.title: Celtics star Jayson Tatum starts in his season debut against the Mavericks
item.description: Jason Tatum is available to play in Celtics’ home matchup with the Dallas Mavericks Friday, almost 10 months after having surgery to repair a ruptured right Achilles tendon.

item.title: BSO ends maestro Andris Nelsons' contract
item.description: The Boston Symphony Orchestra's CEO Chad Smith and Board of Trustees said it was "not aligned on future vision" with Nelsons in a statement emailed to WBUR.

item.title: This weekend’s clock change is a problem, and there’s a deep divide on how to fix it
item.description: Even though polls show most people dislike the system that has most Americans changing clocks twice a year, the political moves necessary to change the system haven't succeeded because opinions on the issue and its potential impacts are sharply divided.

item.title: For a Kurdish family in Maine, hopes of regime change in Iran
item.description: “There are millions of Kurds within Iran ready for this moment,” said Hawreh Haddadi.

item.title: Celtics star Jayson Tatum filled with 'gratitude' in his return to court following Achilles surgery
item.description: Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum’s belated birthday present to himself was a return to the game that was abruptly taken away from him last season. His homecoming at TD Garden on Friday night, a 120-100 victory over the Dallas Mavericks marked his season debut almost 10 months after having surgery to repair a ruptured right Achilles tendon.

item.title: Repost: Change Is A Work In Progress
item.description: Seventeen-year-old “Struggling” had big dreams to leave his small town, but his living situation was at risk because he couldn’t stop using drugs. A letter writer who called herself “Bad Mom” loved her children, but could no longer bear the demands of motherhood. Both desperately needed to transform their lives. item.title: Andris Nelsons out as music director of Boston Symphony at end of 2026-27 season
item.description: Andris Nelsons is leaving as music director of the Boston Symphony Orchestra after the board decides not to renew him. The orchestra says Friday that leaders and Nelsons do not share the same long-term vision. Nelsons tells musicians he did not expect the decision.

item.title: The Latest: Iran accused of attacks in UAE and Bahrain, smoke blankets Tehran from Israeli strikes
item.description: Israel has escalated its war with Iran with strikes in Lebanon and Tehran, and Iran has hit sensitive water sites in the Gulf. On Sunday, Israeli attacks ignited oil storage facilities in Tehran and left the capital under smoke.
